task.description: Design (only) the .zig provenance-citation marking convention that demotes ~200 files / hundreds-to-low-thousands of R-Co .zig source-path citations across lib/ moduledocs and docs/ from live-decision-authority framing to clearly historical provenance, without deleting or altering any citation's path text, and to produce a chunking recommendation for REQ-238 (lib/) and REQ-239 (docs/). No citation is edited by this requirement.
acceptance_criteria: the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req237-*.md) states the exact marker text/regex as a single copy-pasteable string or pattern, with a worked before/after example quoting one real citation from the current tree rewritten under the new convention

the design explicitly confirms the marker is machine-greppable as one regex covering both the moduledoc and markdown contexts, or states a second regex for the markdown context and justifies why unification was not possible

the design does not delete or alter any existing file-path text in its worked example -- the original R-Co path string is fully preserved inside the new marker, confirmed by diffing the before/after example

the design states a concrete chunking recommendation (by directory or subsystem) for REQ-238 and REQ-239's apply steps, sized so no single recommended chunk exceeds what REQ-232 through REQ-236 each treated as one ELIXIR-DEV turn (comparable file count)

CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR signs off per its normal gate: no implementation code in the artefact, every constraint in this requirement's description addressed, unambiguous enough for REQ-238/239 to apply without further design judgement calls

result.note: Design artefact written to lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md. Marker: 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' inserted as a standalone line immediately above the smallest enclosing citation unit (single line, paragraph, or whole table -- structural rule, no per-citation semantic judgement call). Single literal-string regex (`PROVENANCE \(historical, not current decision authority\):`) covers both @moduledoc and docs/ Markdown contexts identically -- no second convention needed, justified in §2(c). Worked example uses REQ-231's own real cursor.zig/field_grants.zig SOURCE: citation (docs/requirements.yaml:13810-13811) plus a second example on lib/letflow/identity.ex's inline moduledoc prose citation, both with explicit before/after diffs showing the original path text byte-identical. Real-tree research (§1) surveyed 5 distinct citation phrasings (SOURCE:, CONTRACT SOURCE:, inline prose, bulleted scope note, table cell) across lib/ (183 files) and docs/ (58 files excl. requirements.yaml, which alone has 538 matching lines) -- no single canonical form exists, confirmed by direct grep rather than assumed. Chunking recommendation (§6): REQ-238 (lib/letflow/, excl. design/, 83 files) split into 8 subsystem chunks of 4-14 files (238a routers 13, 238b engine-core ~14, 238c engine-lua/wasm ~4, 238d definitions 14, 238e api+plugs 10, 238f identity+oidc 9, 238g event_store 5, 238h misc 8), mirroring REQ-232 through REQ-236/240-242's own real measured file counts (4-13 files/turn) as the sizing reference. REQ-239 (docs/) split into 8 chunks: requirements.yaml quartered by REQ-id range (~135 matching lines each, since it is one 538-line-match file), docs/migration/ as one 15-file chunk, docs/issues/ (33 files) halved by ISS-id range, and docs/status/+frontend/+anti-patterns.md as one 10-file chunk. Three open questions flagged explicitly (not silently resolved): OQ-1 marker-styling-vs-greppability trade-off, OQ-2 chunk file/line counts will drift by fix time (exact re-derivation commands given), OQ-3 this design deliberately does not distinguish index-table citations from justification-prose citations, marking both uniformly per the requirement's own 'no per-citation judgement call' instruction. No implementation code included -- all code-fenced blocks in the artefact are quoted real text (before/after prose, diffs, grep commands), not Elixir/script logic.
